**I recovered the March interview, but not the corrected workbook, separate courier receipt or March-specific evidence index.** The available records document a correction; they do not establish whether it changed a caller attribution.

[:chatgpt-content-reference{index="7"}](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_15c936226bb48191bcdff9448f859e46&account_id=personal)

The nine-page report contains the version comparison, field definitions, exact identifiers, original-source links and unsuccessful searches.

### What the March record establishes

The **March 28, 2002 Rugg/Phillips interview**, transcribed **April 23**, says Oracle-to-Excel conversion altered the **last digit of credit-card numbers**. It records receipt of the corrected spreadsheet on **March 29**, via **Airborne Express 50588655-972**. This is the FBI’s receipt statement, not a recovered carrier delivery receipt. The verified pages are **REQ. #35-13 000000350–351**, reproduced at Packet 5 pp. **122–123**. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

| Version | Verified record and remaining limit |
|---|---|
| **November 2001** | Email identifies **UAL_flt93.xls**, under **1A-1A65562**. A handwritten annotation records November 6 FedEx receipt. Three associated table scans were inspected; native workbook bytes remain missing. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"} |
| **March 2002** | Correction and shipment documented; attachment filename, native contents and exact accession remain unlocated. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"} |
| **June/July 2002** | **M-INT-00162543 / …302-116622**, interview June 28, report July 1, defines **28 fields** and describes an updated attachment. That attachment was not recovered. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"} |

**Attribution:** The March report expressly says **Beamer’s name already appeared on the initial spreadsheet**. That weighs against the claim that this correction introduced his name. It does not establish that every attribution was unaffected. Determining that requires matched native call keys, before-and-after values and the supporting attribution records. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}

### Star-Fix originals

FBI-hosted scans now establish that both witnesses supplied handwritten statements: **PDF pp. 31–34, Bates 156–159, lead SF162**. These are **typed reports quoting the statements**, not the handwriting originals. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="5"}

The manager’s [Commission interview, p. 2](https://catalog.archives.gov/medialz/legislative/rg-148/2524787/2610691_Belme.pdf) leaves unresolved which note set went to FBI. The original sheets, intake receipts and United transmittal remain missing. Both original Commission interview recordings were located; **I did not independently listen to them**.

content.text:
Please conduct deep research on the WTC 7 structural explanation. Locate NIST's original reports, available model inputs and outputs, public technical corrections, and the University of Alaska Fairbanks WTC 7 study and model materials. Compare their specific assumptions and predictions concerning column 79, connection failures, thermal expansion, observed interior and exterior timing, and the approximately free-fall interval. Identify observations that discriminate between the models, what each model actually demonstrates, whether model data allow independent reproduction, and the strongest limitations and alternative interpretations. Build on your earlier work and identify any model you did not independently rerun. Disagreement with one explanation does not itself prove an alternative.

Use public material only. Cite exact original sources, document dates, identifiers and page numbers. Separate observations, inferences, contradictory evidence, unsuccessful searches and missing primary records. Do not contact people or custodians, submit requests, incur fees, or disclose private correspondence or litigation strategy.

items.text:
[:chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"}](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_bbac81b618748191bf28a1898cf6c463&account_id=personal)

**The visible collapse sequence is better established than the precise initiating mechanism.** The 12-page review separates observations, model-dependent conclusions, contradictory evidence, unsuccessful searches and missing records, with original-source links, document dates and page references.

The strongest findings:

- **NIST’s timing agreement is mixed.** Relative to east-penthouse descent, its preferred simulation starts north-roof descent at **6.3 seconds versus 6.9 observed**, but makes the west penthouse disappear **2.0–2.4 seconds early**. The reported **2.25-second free-fall interval** concerns a measured north-roof trajectory within a **5.4-second observation interval**; it neither describes the entire collapse nor independently validates the simulation. — *NCSTAR 1A*, November 2008, pp. 42–46. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

- **The fixed-column criticism requires qualification.** NIST’s preliminary floor analysis fixed columns; its full 16-story analysis permitted column movement. The more consequential unresolved questions concern C79 bearing, stiffeners, connection contact and the transition from local failures to global collapse. NIST’s 2020 response discusses these objections but supplies no independently runnable, paired sensitivity demonstration. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

- **UAF demonstrates responses to selected assumptions and imposed support losses.** Its fitted descent does not establish what caused those losses or exclude every fire mechanism. A new archive check joins final-report figures to identifiable job families: one associated input uses **8.2 × 10⁻⁶/°F**, while the report describes an adverse thermal-expansion test using **11.5 × 10⁻⁶/°F**. That requires version reconciliation; it is not proof that every UAF result is invalid. Exact files, hashes and qualifications appear on report pp. 6 and 12.

- **The most useful discriminators** are C79 connection behavior under documented thermal histories, synchronized interior/exterior event timing, and independently predicted multi-point roof motion—not visual resemblance alone.

**I did not independently rerun NIST, UAF or OpenSees models.** I inspected selected public inputs and logs and recalculated published velocity regressions; I did not retrack original video. UAF’s archive is accessible, but exact final-run provenance remains incomplete. Critical NIST native inputs/results remain withheld. Neither limitation proves an alternative explanation.

Deep research follow-up: Flight 93 maintenance notes and the WTC K-13 cutting and accession records.

Start by inventorying what the investigation already holds and what has already been requested. Check the actual scope and status of prior Flight 93 Airfone and Hangar 17 requests if available, and distinguish a sent request or acknowledgment from a production. If you cannot access the current tracker, identify exactly what needs checking before any draft could be used. Search public primary sources and archives for the missing records before drafting a new request.

1. Flight 93: Start with the Commission interviews of the Star-Fix operator (NAID 2609596) and maintenance manager (NAID 2610691). Seek the manager's two sets of notes, the operator's contemporaneous written statement, the FBI evidence receipt or intake, and any United transmittal or Commission copy. Compare 9:30, 9:35 and 9:40 Eastern and keep carrier connection, queue, desk answer, manager takeover and relay to Chicago distinct. Look for the native call keys, clock definitions and worksheet only where they can resolve the discrepancy. Starting review: https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/1e4baca5c7b93418afab59edf60a4776d85feae6/investigation/broader-evidence/telephone-ua93-starfix-maintenance-2026-11-06/README.md

2. K-13: Start with museum accession C.2009.310.6, NIST's K-1 or K-13 North Tower panel, the separately listed July 29, 2002 K-13 flange coupon, and the column 210 specimens in NCSTAR 1-3C Figure 6-14. Seek the accession and condition files, Port Authority transfer/tag records, original intake photos, the coupon transmittal and parent-piece cutting log, sample-preparation identifiers, and the FEMA source row or NIST crosswalk that could explain the conflicting FEMA-match entries. Require dated specimen identifiers or compatible markings and geometry for each join. Starting review: https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/fe6c52e9cc375b3b6958ef8ae8aaa41f537e2892/investigation/broader-evidence/steel-k13-panel-coupon-crosswalk-2026-11-06/README.md

Deliver a source-cited findings and request-coverage table, contrary evidence, failed searches, and a draft for each material gap not already covered. For each draft identify the likely custodian, exact identifiers, records sought, and the prior request or search it supplements. Keep the drafts unsent, with no fee authorization. Do not contact custodians, submit requests, or circulate private records.

items.text:
**Two new leads narrow the gaps, but neither custody chain is closed.**

**Flight 93:** Public FBI-report reproductions contain typed transcriptions of handwritten statements reportedly supplied by the operator and manager. The manager’s approximately **06:40 passage describes taking over an existing call**; his later Commission interview describes it as the estimated start. This helps distinguish stages but does **not reconcile 9:30, 9:35 and 9:40 Eastern**. The original handwriting, identification of the two note sets, FBI intake receipt and United transmittal remain unlocated. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

**K-13:** [FEMA’s original Appendix D](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GOVPUB-FEM1-PURL-LPS18973/pdf/GOVPUB-FEM1-PURL-LPS18973.pdf#page=276) supplies concrete leads: row 106 records **December 20, 2001, Bonilla Photo 5, a Massa coupon photograph and a GMS destination**. Row 101 records a **93–96** floor marking, whereas NIST identifies **97–100**. That could explain the conflicting FEMA-match entries; the reconciliation worksheet is still missing. No verified chain connects those rows, the July 2002 coupon, column 210 samples and museum accession. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

### Verified request coverage

| Existing request | Actual status | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| [NARA Airfone](https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#all/1a1ae8b11b1bccbe) | Sent; automatic receipt only | Carrier packages already requested; notes/intake not expressly covered. |
| [NIST contractor records](https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#all/1a1805fab72800db) | Sent; no agency response or production located | Photos/crosswalks may overlap; draft targets specimen cutting/preparation records. |
| [Hangar 17](https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#all/1a1ae9c8ed45cc50) | Sent; no acknowledgment or production located | Scope concerns asbestos sampling and associated artifact crosswalks. |
| [Earlier NARA response](https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#all/1a1a89a314d48f9a) | **2020 finding aid received** | This is not production of the underlying requested records. |

The report contains the full inventory, timing and specimen tables, contrary evidence, failed searches, inaccessible-original limitations, and **seven complete unsent drafts**.

Separately seek the FBI van-sample final chemistry accession, controls, result and disposition; do not substitute a canine alert or NIST's lack of tower-steel residue testing for a laboratory result. items.text:
**The original steel inventories and actual UAF inputs are now verified. Same-specimen chemical confirmation and final van chemistry remain unverified.**

- **Chemical replication:** Jones’s recovered [2012 statement](https://web.archive.org/web/20120930141521/http://911blogger.com/news/2012-09-08/letter-regarding-redgray-chip-analyses) reports inconclusive aluminum-phase identification by TEM and outside-laboratory XRD. I located no completed independent confirmation on authenticated retained Harrit specimens or documented splits. Same-donor dust, different chips and synthetic comparison materials do not establish that replication.

- **FEMA provenance:** The [original spreadsheet, PDF p. 270](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GOVPUB-FEM1-PURL-LPS18973/pdf/GOVPUB-FEM1-PURL-LPS18973.pdf#page=270), identifies A/W14A, B/W14B and C12a/b. NIST’s inventory lists the first two as unidentified steel. **Neither is authenticated as Appendix C Sample 1.** Trip dates and note takers are not established recovery dates or collectors. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

- **UAF archive:** I inventoried **22,238 entries** and integrity-checked ten selected files. Historical logs distinguish an externally interrupted local run, a nonconvergent local run and a completed global run. **No model or sensitivity sweep was rerun.** The archive identifies itself with the 2019 draft; correspondence to final-report figures remains unresolved.

- **FBI van:** Fabric, blanket samples and glove/bomb-suit controls are documented under **E01889035/36/37**. No matched chemistry accession, final sample/control results or item-specific disposition was recovered. The [2005 memo, PDF p. 89](https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/main/investigation/urban-moving-systems/fbi-van-lab-release-2026-10-06/raw/section-6.pdf#page=89), announces future property destruction; it does not certify destruction of those samples. Neither a canine alert nor NIST’s testing omission supplies a laboratory result.

Authenticated pre-collapse attachment to mapped steel, specimen-specific chemistry, and corrosion demonstrably preceding fracture would materially favor installation. Early dust collection can exclude later cleanup processes but cannot alone establish installation. **No reviewed evidence attributes installation to UMS or Max.**

The updated report identifies inaccessible originals, missing data and computational limits; new findings occupy **pp. 13–18**. No one was contacted.

content.text:
# Deep-research prompts: UMS, Saudi leads and WTC evidence

November 5, 2026. These prompts can be pasted individually into a research tool. They are prioritized by how directly the requested records could test a missing connection. They request research and analysis only: do not contact people, submit requests, authorize fees, publish or transmit private files without separate authorization. A reference to a pending request is a lead, not proof it covers a record or that an agency located it; inspect the current tracker and receipts before proposing any supplement.


## 6. WTC physical evidence and alternative models

```text
Independently assess the most probative physical evidence for and against pre-planted explosives or incendiaries at WTC 1, 2 and 7, keeping each building and sample separate. Compare FEMA's 2002 Appendix C steel observations and alternative causes; Harrit et al.'s 2009 red/gray-chip paper; Millette's 2012 work on different samples; the NIST tower and WTC 7 reports and FAQs; and UAF's WTC 7 study, model files and funding disclosures.

For each item identify specimen origin, chain of custody, collection date, analytic techniques, observed data, controls, timing uncertainties, competing explanations, independent same-specimen replication and documented limitations. Distinguish corrosion or elemental presence from identification of an installed charge. Compare predicted and observed structural, video, audio and seismic signatures, the inputs and assumptions of NIST and UAF models, and sensitivity to disputed assumptions. Treat NIST's 2.25-second WTC 7 north-face free-fall interval within its full timeline, and separately note NIST's statement that it did not test tower steel for explosive or thermite residues. Neither alone proves demolition. Avoid treating a WTC 7 model as a model of the towers.

Explain which specific observations would materially favor or weaken each hypothesis, and whether any physical evidence attributes responsibility to UMS or Max Movers. Cite original reports and pages, and distinguish findings from model-dependent inferences and unknowns. Do not provide procedures for manufacturing or testing dangerous energetic materials.
```
